target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to SharePoint file send requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MS Teams group/channel file sends that could hang indefinitely when SharePoint upload, sharing-link creation, chat-member lookup, or drive-item metadata requests stalled before headers or while reading response bodies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The affected SharePoint/Graph calls now use an aborting timeout around the full fetch lifecycle, including response body reads. The timeout helper lives in `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`, the existing MS Teams timeout owner.

SharePoint content PUTs now use the same size-aware transfer policy as the adjacent MS Teams file-consent upload path: a 5 minute base stall bound plus transfer budget at 256 KiB/s. Short Graph control-plane requests keep the existing 30 second MS Teams request timeout so stalled metadata/link/member calls still fail quickly without cutting off slow but valid file uploads.

## User Impact

MS Teams group/channel file sends no longer remain pending forever when Microsoft Graph or SharePoint stops responding. Slow valid large uploads get a transfer-sized deadline instead of being cut off by a fixed 5 minute ceiling or the 30 second control-plane timeout.

## Evidence

Exact head: `5a4dc3f94616aab7df490411c3237242aa0ca932`.

Latest implementation update after ClawSweeper review:

- Replaced the fixed `MSTEAMS_SHAREPOINT_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000` ceiling with `resolveMSTeamsSharePointUploadTimeoutMs(sizeInBytes)`.
- The resolver matches the adjacent MS Teams file-consent policy: 5 minute base stall bound plus size-derived transfer budget at 256 KiB/s.
- `uploadToSharePoint()` now passes `params.buffer.length` into the resolver for the SharePoint content PUT.
- Graph control-plane calls (`createLink`, chat members, drive item metadata) still use the default 30 second request timeout.
- Added regression coverage for a 250 MiB resolver budget, slow large upload success after the 5 minute base bound, and abort after the size-aware transfer budget.

Validation run locally as a narrow fallback for this fork PR; GitHub CI will rerun on the pushed head:

```text
git diff --check
-> clean

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts
-> 2 files passed, 15 tests passed

scripts/committer "fix(msteams): size SharePoint upload deadline by file length" extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts
-> committed 5a4dc3f94616aab7df490411c3237242aa0ca932
```

Autoreview status:

```text
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local
TMPDIR=$(pwd)/../autoreview-tmp .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local
-> both attempts failed before producing structured JSON review output:
   codex engine failed (1); helper refused PATH aliases under the temporary codex runtime directory.
```

This is not counted as a clean autoreview result.

Controlled partial SharePoint/Graph stalled-transport proof retained from the prior exact-head-equivalent run:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module
```

Harness shape: production `uploadAndShareSharePoint()` / `uploadToSharePoint()` helpers, real Node HTTP loopback server, real `fetch()` transport to loopback, redacted token provider, and a transport shim that redirects Microsoft Graph/SharePoint URLs to loopback paths. This is intentionally not described as a live Microsoft tenant run.

Redacted transcript:


Observed behavior:

- Slow SharePoint upload that finishes after 31s succeeds; the 30s control-plane timeout does not abort content upload.
- Stalled SharePoint `createLink` control-plane request still rejects after about 30s and the server observes socket close.
- Stalled SharePoint content upload rejects and closes the server socket after the upload transfer deadline.
- Latest focused tests additionally prove the fixed 5 minute upload ceiling was removed for large files: a 250 MiB upload gets 300000ms + 1000000ms of budget at 256 KiB/s, and production `uploadToSharePoint()` does not abort a slow large transfer at the 5 minute base bound.

Known limits:

- This proof runs production MS Teams graph-upload helpers through real HTTP loopback stalls/success, but it is still not a live Microsoft Graph/SharePoint tenant proof.
- No Microsoft tenant credentials were available in this environment, so a real group/channel file send against Microsoft services remains untested.
- Remote credentialed Testbox was intentionally not used for this fork PR; validation used narrow local fallback plus GitHub CI on the pushed branch.
